title: The Parrot Episode
summary: Josh and Chuck explore parrots: the roughly 350-400 species of the order, their physical traits (curved beak, zygodactyl feet, pigments with antibacterial properties), wild range including feral populations in the US, extinct North American species like the Carolina parakeet and passenger pigeon, the New Zealand kea attacking sheep, the kākāpō's nocturnal habits, and parrot social life and communication. They cover mating and parental care, tool use by cockatoos and greater vasa parrots, altruism experiments with African greys, mimicry and dialects, Alex the parrot and Puck, parrots as pets and pirates, the illegal bird trade and extinction threats, and listener mail from Vivek Gower.

segments.title: Opening banter and parrot introduction
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with banter about parrots, their surprising intelligence, and personal anecdotes about parrots and bird people. They note birds are the fourth most popular pet in the US.

segments.title: Parrot diversity and physical traits
segments.summary: They discuss the nearly 400 parrot species, size range from the kakapo-like Coca poa to tiny New Guinea species, colorful plumage and its pigments with antibacterial properties, the zygodactyl toe arrangement, and the powerful beak.

segments.title: Parrot social behavior and the Yuma cafe anecdote
segments.summary: They discuss how parrots accept members of their flock but attack outsiders, with a story about parrots at an outdoor cafe in Yuma, Arizona, and a claim that a large parrot can snap a broomstick.

segments.title: Sponsor break
segments.summary: Short promotional break for other podcasts.

segments.title: Wild parrot range and the Carolina parakeet
segments.summary: Parrots live in tropical and southern regions and adapt to other climates. Feral parrots live in the US, including Pasadena and Hyde Park. The Carolina parakeet and passenger pigeon were driven to extinction, and the last of each died at the Cincinnati Zoo.

segments.title: Kea attacks on sheep and feral parrots in US cities
segments.summary: Kea in New Zealand were found in the mid-1800s to attack sheep. Conservation efforts include repellent on sheep. Pasadena parrots have disrupted film shoots. Feral populations occur in Florida, Texas, California, and Chicago.

segments.title: Parrot family life, mating, and pandemonium communication
segments.summary: Parrots are generally monogamous, with both parents raising chicks; incubation is 18 to 30 days and young may stay up to four years. Flocks communicate with calls. Lovebirds reform bonds by feeding one another.

segments.title: Parrot tool use, altruism, and mimicry
segments.summary: Cockatoos use sticks to drum on logs in courtship; greater vasa parrots grind shells with pebbles for courtship feeding. African greys showed reciprocal altruism in a token exchange study. Parrots are known for mimicry, including a bird mimicking a camera sound.

segments.title: Parrot speech, dialects, and Chuck's cockatiel Dolly
segments.summary: Parrots form regional vocal dialects and can adjust accents. Parrots can mimic human speech by manipulating the tongue. Chuck describes teaching his cockatiel Dolly to talk and whistle.

segments.title: Alex the parrot, Puck, and parrot cognition
segments.summary: Alex the parrot, studied by Irene Pepperberg, understood zero, bigger and smaller, and same and different, knew about a hundred words, and reportedly asked what color when seeing himself in a mirror. Puck held the record for most words.

segments.title: Pirates, parrot history, and parrot as pets
segments.summary: Parrots on pirate ships are plausible but unverified. Europe's parrot fashion began with Alexander the Great's return from India and revived with trips to Brazil. Parrots are demanding, messy, and long-lived, with Cookie the cockatoo living to 83.

segments.title: Illegal bird trade, extinction threats, and conservation
segments.summary: Around 800,000 parrot chicks a year are removed from nests for the exotic bird market, many dying in transit. A 2021 study found a third of species threatened. Hotspots and US anti-poaching legislation are discussed.

segments.title: Listener mail from Vivek Gower
segments.summary: Listener Vivek Gower, a physiotherapist in Delhi, writes that he listens during his commute and launched his own podcast. The hosts invite listeners to email the show.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck close the episode and thank listeners.
